I've been working this land for 45 years and I know Quzhou's soil and climate well. My 12 mu breaks down as 8 mu in wheat-maize rotation and 4 mu dedicated to cotton — cotton needs the full growing season from April to October, so it can't share ground with the wheat-maize cycle.

**Wheat (8 mu, October through June):** I'll use an improved variety — probably Kenong 199, which performs reliably in Quzhou's conditions. With my education I've tracked yield trials and this variety holds up well against late-season heat. Base fertilizer goes in at planting, urea top-dress at jointing. I'll irrigate three times: the winter water to protect roots during dormancy, jointing stage, and grain fill. Two pesticide passes — a herbicide in early tillering and an aphid/fungicide spray near heading. I'll rotary till after maize harvest in September.

**Maize (8 mu, June through September, same plots):** After wheat harvest I go straight in with no-till seeding — saves time and moisture, and at my age I'm not ploughing twice a year when I don't need to. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the seed station has that season. Fertilize at planting and a top-dress at V6. Two irrigations, one at silking. Two pesticide passes for borer and armyworm.

**Cotton (4 mu, April through October):** Deep plough in early spring to break the pan layer — cotton roots need depth. Hybrid Bt cotton reduces bollworm pressure substantially, so I can cut pesticide passes to three rather than the old five or six. I split nitrogen across three applications: base, boll set, and late boll opening. Four irrigations spaced through the season. Cotton is my main cash crop; the wheat-maize feeds the household and covers inputs.
